text:
Richard Stallman is a prominent activist known for championing the free software movement. His core philosophy centers on software freedom, which he advocates for through his GNU project, initiated in September 1983 with the goal of creating a free operating system compatible with Unix. He established the Free Software Foundation (FSF) as a non-profit organization to support the movement and popularized the concept of copyleft, first implemented in the GNU Emacs General Public License and later in the GNU General Public License (GPL).
Stallman is a vocal political campaigner against digital rights management (DRM), software patents, and proprietary software. He proposes concepts like "reduced copyright" and suggests that non-commercial sharing of copies should not be a copyright violation. Regarding terminology, he insists on using "free software" and "GNU/Linux," arguing against the terms "intellectual property" and "piracy." Despite criticism and personal controversies, he announced his return to the FSF board of directors in March 2021.
